newsitem.title: UK: UK to crack down on electrical goods pricing.
newsitem.headline: UK to crack down on electrical goods pricing.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Wednesday that it planned to prohibit recommended retail prices, which it said were distorting the domestic electrical goods retail market.

"I have accepted the unanimous findings of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission that a variety of widespread and entrenched practices by suppliers and dealers of domestic electrical goods operate against the public interest," DTI president Margaret Beckett said in a statement.
Beckett said the MMC had discovered that consumers were paying more than they should for white goods because new retailers had difficulty getting supplies and innovation was discouraged.

"I propose to implement a package of remedies which will stop suppliers and dealers from relying on recommended retail prices...consumers will benefit from lower prices through stronger price competition and more choice of retail outlets," she said.
Beckett said she planned to stop suppliers making agreements which restrict dealers' freedom to advertise and sell goods at prices lower than those considered appropriate by suppliers.
Beckett said the MMC believed recommended retail prices were so entrenched that prohibition was the only solution to effect a change in the electrical goods market.
